Subject: Cirrus Health follow-up — commercial path & procurement next steps

Hi Samir —

Great call earlier — appreciate you and the team walking through the use cases and procurement constraints. Short recap and suggested next steps so procurement has what they need to decide between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private:

Recap (key decision points)
- Procurement preference: purchase via PO/invoice (Net terms) rather than corporate card.
- Marketplace: Cirrus is open to Marketplace if it supports PO/EIN invoicing and does not force card checkout.
- Deployment fit: initial pilot can run on Hosted (lower lift) with the option to move to Dedicated if we hit predictable high throughput or want dedicated capacity and isolation. Private (VPC/on-prem) is a later-stage conversation for regulatory enclaves.
- Commit vs on-demand: procurement asks about commit tiers and whether committed discounts and monthly invoicing are available.

What I will send (attached)
- Draft SOW for a 3-month pilot + optional 12-month renewal (RDW_SOW_draft_v1.pdf)
- Pricing matrix with hosted/dedicated/private rows and commit vs on-demand columns (cirrus_pricing_matrix_v2.xlsx)

Questions to you / procurement
1) Will Cirrus accept Net30/Net45/Net60? If Net60, any internal approvals needed that would affect timeline?
2) Do you want us to propose a Marketplace SKU (AWS Marketplace) versus direct invoicing? If Marketplace, we need to align onboarding flow and expected invoice to vendor mapping.
3) Any required procurement documents we should include with the SOW (W-9, certificate of insurance, vendor form)?

Next steps
- I’ll send the two attachments now.
- Can we set a procurement call with your procurement lead early next week (suggest Wed 12/22 10:00 AM PT)?
- If procurement prefers a PO + committed discount, we’ll propose a 12-month commit option with pricing tiers (and a fall-back month-to-month on-demand rate).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the attachments in a separate email and include the HubSpot deal link so we can track approvals.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra

Rishi — thanks for the recap and for sending the files. Quick clarifications from my side after reviewing the pricing matrix:

- Procurement: we do prefer to flow via PO and invoice; Net30 is typical but I need to confirm if Net60 is possible (some of our hospitals run Net60). Procurement will chime in.
- Marketplace: we like the idea if it preserves a PO-to-invoice experience and if billing lands against our company entity (not individual card). Can Redwood invoice via AWS Marketplace or do you force card-based purchases there?
- Commit size: for a pilot we likely won’t commit to 12 months up front. We’re more likely to do a 3-month paid pilot with an option to convert to a 12-month commit if performance and unit economics make sense. If you can surface a 3-month pilot price + an optional conversion credit that’d be ideal.

Also — timeline: procurement will need W-9 and vendor form; I’ll pull our procurement lead into the thread.

If possible, can you include an example PO language snippet we typically need to drop into our system (billing address, EIN, invoice cadence)? That will speed approvals.

Appreciate it,
Samir
Head of Platform, Cirrus Health
samir@cirrushealth.com

Team — quick internal note so we’re aligned before the procurement call:

Summary of ask
- Cirrus will onboard via PO/invoice. They favor a PO-driven flow and need W-9 + vendor packet. Marketplace is acceptable only if it supports PO invoicing (no card-forced signup).
- Pilot preference: 3-month paid pilot with option to convert to a 12-month commit. Procurement may approve Net30; Net60 needs higher approval.

Proposed commercial options to present
1) Pilot-first (recommended)
   - 3-month paid pilot on Hosted (on-demand) at a blended pilot rate.
   - Conversion option: credit applied to first invoice if they convert to a 12-month commit within 60 days.
2) Commit-first (if they prefer predictable economics)
   - 12-month commit with ~18% committed discount for Hosted. Dedicated pricing available as add-on; we can propose a dedicated pool for production after pilot.
3) Private/VPC — provide as a third option in SOW but note longer lead time and separate procurement review.

Operational items we will send
- W-9, Redwood remit information, sample PO language (I’ll draft), and the SOW + pricing we already attached (RDW_SOW_draft_v1.pdf, cirrus_pricing_matrix_v2.xlsx).
- Legal: propose Net30 standard; flag Net60 for commercial acceptance only if signoff from Revenue Ops.

Next steps
- I’ll schedule procurement onboarding call for Wed 12/22 10:00 AM PT (tentative). Rishi — can you confirm availability and send the HubSpot link in the calendar invite so we have the deal attached?
- Aditya — can you confirm the conversion credit terms we can offer (e.g., apply pilot payments pro-rata to committed contract within 60 days)?

Thanks,
Monica Patel
